description: An introduction to physical quantities, fundamental and derived quantities, SI units and prefixes, and the instruments and methods used to measure length, mass, time, temperature and volume.

options.text: A quantity that cannot be measured
A quantity that can be measured

mcq.explanation: A physical quantity is any quantity that can be measured, such as length, mass and time. Exam Tip: A physical quantity has a NUMBER and a UNIT (e.g. 5 metres).

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a fundamental (basic) physical quantity?
mcq.explanation: Length is fundamental, while area, volume and speed are derived from other quantities. Exam Tip: Fundamental quantities are length, mass and time; built-up quantities such as area and speed are derived.

mcq.questionText: The SI unit of length is the:
mcq.explanation: The SI unit of length is the metre. Exam Tip: length is measured in metre (m), mass in kilogram (kg) and time in second (s).

mcq.questionText: The SI unit of mass is the:
mcq.explanation: The SI unit of mass is the kilogram. Exam Tip: the newton measures force, not mass.

mcq.questionText: The SI unit of time is the:
mcq.explanation: The SI unit of time is the second. Exam Tip: hours and minutes are used daily, but the second is the SI base unit.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a derived quantity?
mcq.explanation: Area = length x length, so it is a derived quantity. Exam Tip: derived quantities include area, volume, speed, density, force and pressure.

mcq.questionText: The instrument used to measure the length of a football field is a:
mcq.explanation: A long flexible tape measure is suited to measuring large lengths. Exam Tip: use a tape for large lengths, a ruler for cm/mm, a vernier caliper for about 0.01 cm and a micrometer for about 0.01 mm.

mcq.questionText: The instrument used to measure the mass of an object is the:
mcq.explanation: A beam or electronic balance measures mass. Exam Tip: balance measures mass, ruler measures length, stopwatch measures time and thermometer measures temperature.

mcq.questionText: Which instrument is most suitable for measuring the diameter of a thin wire accurately?
mcq.explanation: A micrometer screw gauge measures very small lengths, down to 0.01 mm. Exam Tip: the micrometer gives the smallest measurements, while the vernier caliper suits slightly larger small objects.

mcq.questionText: The SI unit of temperature is the:
mcq.explanation: The SI unit of temperature is the kelvin (K). Exam Tip: the SI unit is the kelvin (K), though degrees Celsius are common in the lab.

mcq.questionText: The instrument used to measure time intervals in an experiment is a:
mcq.explanation: A stopwatch measures time intervals. Exam Tip: a stopwatch measures time in seconds, while a protractor measures angles.

mcq.questionText: The volume of a liquid can be measured accurately using a:
mcq.explanation: A measuring cylinder has a graduated scale for reading volume. Exam Tip: read at the BOTTOM of the meniscus, at eye level, to avoid parallax error.
The prefix kilo means one thousand, that is a factor of 1000. Exam Tip: kilo = 1000, milli = 1/1000 and centi = 1/100.

mcq.questionText: How many centimetres are there in 1 metre?
mcq.explanation: Centi means one hundredth, so 1 m = 100 cm. Exam Tip: remember 1 m = 100 cm = 1000 mm.

mcq.questionText: The volume of an irregular solid, such as a small stone, can be found using a measuring cylinder by the method of:
mcq.explanation: Lowering the solid into water and reading the rise in level gives its volume. Exam Tip: volume of an irregular solid = final water level - initial water level.

fib.questionText: A quantity that can be measured is called a ____ quantity.
fib.explanation: Any quantity that can be measured, such as length or mass, is a physical quantity. Exam Tip: a physical quantity always has a number and a unit.

fib.questionText: Quantities such as length, mass and time, from which other quantities are obtained, are called ____ quantities.
fib.explanation: Length, mass and time are the basic building blocks, so they are fundamental quantities. Exam Tip: fundamental quantities include length, mass, time, temperature and current.

fib.questionText: The SI unit of length is the ____.
fib.explanation: The metre (m) is the SI base unit of length. Exam Tip: the metre (m) is the SI base unit of length.

fib.questionText: Quantities obtained by combining fundamental quantities, such as area and speed, are called ____ quantities.
fib.explanation: Area and speed are built from fundamental quantities, so they are derived. Exam Tip: area, volume, speed, density, force and pressure are all derived.

fib.questionText: The instrument used to measure very small lengths, such as the thickness of a coin, to 0.01 mm is the ____.
fib.explanation: The micrometer screw gauge reads to 0.01 mm, making it ideal for very small lengths. Exam Tip: the micrometer (0.01 mm) is more precise than the vernier caliper (0.01 cm).

fib.questionText: The SI unit of mass is the ____.
fib.explanation: The kilogram (kg) is the SI base unit of mass. Exam Tip: do not confuse mass (kg) with weight (newton).

fib.questionText: The prefix "milli" means one ____ of a unit.
fib.explanation: Milli means one thousandth, so 1 mm = 1/1000 m. Exam Tip: milli means divide by 1000, so 1 mm = 1/1000 m.

fib.questionText: The volume of a regular solid such as a cube is found by multiplying length x width x ____.
fib.explanation: The volume of a cuboid is length x width x height. Exam Tip: regular solids use formulas, while irregular solids use water displacement.

fib.questionText: The instrument used to measure the temperature of a substance is the ____.
fib.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature. Exam Tip: the thermometer measures temperature, whose SI unit is the kelvin.

fib.questionText: The volume of an irregularly shaped stone is measured by the method of ____ of water.
fib.explanation: The rise in water level when the stone is submerged equals the stone's volume, the displacement method. Exam Tip: volume = rise in water level = final reading - initial reading.

tf.questionText: A physical quantity can be measured and has a number and a unit.
tf.explanation: A physical quantity always consists of a numerical value together with a unit. Exam Tip: a value without a unit is incomplete in physics.

tf.questionText: Length, mass and time are derived quantities.
tf.explanation: Length, mass and time are fundamental quantities, not derived. Exam Tip: they are fundamental, while area, speed and density are derived.

tf.questionText: The SI unit of mass is the kilogram.
tf.explanation: The kilogram is the SI base unit of mass. Exam Tip: the kilogram (kg) is the base unit for mass.
Speed = distance / time, so it is built from other quantities and is derived. Exam Tip: speed = distance / time, so it is derived.

tf.questionText: A micrometer screw gauge is more precise than a metre rule.
tf.explanation: The micrometer reads to 0.01 mm, far finer than the 1 mm of a metre rule. Exam Tip: micrometer (0.01 mm) is finer than vernier caliper (0.01 cm), which is finer than a ruler (1 mm).
Since centi means one hundredth, 1 m contains 100 cm. Exam Tip: 1 m = 100 cm = 1000 mm.

tf.questionText: The volume of an irregular solid can be found using the water displacement method.
tf.explanation: Submerging the solid raises the water level by an amount equal to its volume. Exam Tip: volume = final water level - initial water level.

tf.questionText: The prefix "kilo" means one thousandth of a unit.
tf.explanation: Kilo means one thousand, not one thousandth; milli means one thousandth. Exam Tip: kilo = 1000 and milli = 1/1000, so they are easily swapped.

tf.questionText: A stopwatch is used to measure time.
tf.explanation: A stopwatch measures time intervals in seconds. Exam Tip: the stopwatch measures time in seconds.

tf.questionText: When reading a measuring cylinder, the eye should be above the liquid, looking down at an angle.
tf.explanation: Reading at an angle causes parallax error; the eye must be level with the liquid. Exam Tip: read at eye level, straight on, at the bottom of the meniscus.

summary.correctAnswer: A quantity that can be measured and is expressed as a number together with a unit, such as 5 metres.
summary.explanation: Examples include length, mass and time. Exam Tip: every physical quantity needs both a number and a unit.

summary.correctAnswer: Basic quantities from which all others are obtained, namely length, mass and time (also temperature and current).
summary.explanation: They are the building blocks of measurement. Exam Tip: remember length, mass and time as the core fundamental quantities.

summary.correctAnswer: Quantities obtained by combining fundamental quantities, such as area, volume, speed, density and force.
summary.explanation: For example area = length x length. Exam Tip: if a quantity is built from other quantities, it is derived.

summary.questionText: SI units of the base quantities
summary.correctAnswer: The metre for length, the kilogram for mass, the second for time and the kelvin for temperature.
summary.explanation: These are the standard international units. Exam Tip: length metre (m), mass kilogram (kg), time second (s), temperature kelvin (K).

summary.correctAnswer: Kilo means one thousand (1000), centi means one hundredth (1/100) and milli means one thousandth (1/1000).
summary.explanation: Prefixes scale a unit up or down. Exam Tip: 1 km = 1000 m, 1 m = 100 cm and 1 m = 1000 mm.

summary.correctAnswer: Tools matched to a quantity: ruler or tape for length, balance for mass, stopwatch for time and thermometer for temperature.
summary.explanation: Choosing the right instrument gives an accurate reading. Exam Tip: match each instrument to the quantity it measures.

summary.correctAnswer: The micrometer screw gauge reads to about 0.01 mm, while the vernier caliper reads to about 0.01 cm, so the micrometer is more precise.
summary.explanation: Both measure small lengths but to different precision. Exam Tip: use the micrometer for the smallest objects and the vernier caliper for slightly larger ones.

summary.correctAnswer: A method for finding the volume of an irregular solid by measuring the rise in water level when it is submerged.
summary.explanation: Volume = final water level - initial water level. Exam Tip: use displacement for irregular solids and formulas for regular ones.

summary.correctAnswer: An error in reading a scale caused by viewing it from an angle instead of straight on at eye level.
summary.explanation: It commonly happens when reading a measuring cylinder. Exam Tip: read at eye level at the bottom of the meniscus to avoid it.

summary.correctAnswer: The curved surface of a liquid in a container, read at its lowest point when measuring volume.
summary.explanation: Water forms a downward curve in a measuring cylinder. Exam Tip: take the reading at the bottom of the meniscus, at eye level.

hoq.questionText: A student pours water into a measuring cylinder up to the 40 cm3 mark, then lowers a small stone in and the level rises to 65 cm3. What is the volume of the stone, and which method?
hoq.explanation: The volume equals the rise in water level, final minus initial, which is 65 - 40 = 25 cm3, found by water displacement. Exam Tip: volume = rise in level (final - initial); option A wrongly ADDS the readings.

hoq.questionText: Classify the following as fundamental or derived: (i) mass, (ii) area, (iii) time, (iv) density.
hoq.explanation: Mass and time are basic, so they are fundamental, while area = length x length and density = mass/volume are built from other quantities, so they are derived. Exam Tip: ask "is it built from other quantities?" If yes, it is derived.

hoq.questionText: A rectangular metal sheet is 8 cm long, 5 cm wide, thickness 2 mm. To find its VOLUME in cubic centimetres, what must she do, and what is the volume?

options.text: Convert 2 mm to 0.2 cm, then 8 x 5 x 0.2 = 8 cm3

hoq.explanation: First convert the thickness 2 mm to 0.2 cm, then multiply volume = 8 x 5 x 0.2 = 8 cm3. Exam Tip: convert every measurement to the SAME unit before multiplying, remembering 10 mm = 1 cm.
